case.title: Azure App Service: intermittent HTTP 503/502 and latency spikes on revenue-critical checkout API (East US)

relatedIncidents.title: App Service: elevated 503/502 and latency in East US (scale-unit networking degradation)
relatedIncidents.summary: A subset of App Service scale units in East US experienced transient networking degradation caused by a faulty network node rotation. Health probes to affected instances intermittently failed, so healthy instances were pulled from rotation, producing intermittent 503/502 responses, elevated P95 latency, and downstream SQL connection timeouts for tenants on those scale units. Impact was intermittent and load-sensitive (worse at peak). Detected 13:42 UTC, mitigated 16:05 UTC by rerouting traffic and recycling degraded nodes, and fully resolved 18:20 UTC. No customer action was required; customers with app-level retries and geo-failover saw minimal impact.
relatedIncidents.mitigation: Rerouted affected scale-unit traffic away from degraded network nodes and recycled the affected nodes; instances returned to healthy rotation.
relatedIncidents.howFixed: Root-caused to a faulty network node rotation on the scale unit. Corrected the rotation, added a guard to prevent the bad state from recurring, and shipped a health-probe fix so healthy instances are no longer pulled during brief network blips.
